name: bums.level.w3-07.name
authorNotes: Two players required — this is the world's team gate, and the pop cannon is the gate. Segment 1 (trapeze-approach, pivot flush with the starting pier's edge) is ordinary: both players cross independently, same as any World 3 trapeze so far. Segment 2 is the real point of the level: pier A2 to pier B2 is 800px, nearly triple a single trapeze's carry, and cannon-gate is the only structure that spans it. The intended play is the one the world has been building to: one player stays anchored on pier A2's edge, reaches out to grip the barrel (the 'handle'), and the other climbs into the barrel mouth as ammunition; the handle-holder's use-item fires whoever's head is inside the barrel bounds, so it is the gripper's press that launches their partner, not their own position, that matters. As a matter of engine honesty (the same note w1-b's tide flagged for its own schema gap): the barrel is one 90px body and a floating hand can reach 118px in any direction from a floating head, so — exactly as 04 demonstrated — a lone player can still fold themselves into the barrel and self-fire solo; nothing in the prop contract can wall that off. What the level actually gates is the gap itself, not the button-press: there is no trapeze, rope or ledge that spans pier A2 to pier B2 on its own (trapeze-final3 in segment 3 is deliberately the world's longest, 350px, and still would not reach this 800px void), so every player who crosses this segment goes through cannon-gate one way or another, and doing it as a pair — one holding, one flying — is the fast, intended, and much funnier way. relic-w3-07 sits just past the gate on pier B2, so the haul objective can't be finished by either player working alone. Segment 3 closes the level: trapeze-final3 swings out and releases onto trampoline-final, a standalone landing pad, which bounces the rest of the way to the goal pier — both players make this crossing solo, same as segment 1. The gate's assist beam is drawn thicker than the others as a visual tell that this is the level's hard point.
